text:
Officials from North Korea and Laos have met in Pyongyang to discuss measures to expand cooperation in the economy, trade, and science and technology sectors, Pyongyang's state media reported Friday.
The fourth session of the joint committee on economic, trade, scientific and technological cooperation was held at the Pyongyang Assembly Hall on Thursday, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said.
Yun Jong-ho, the North's external economic relations minister, led the country's delegation, while Malaithong Kommasith, Laos' industry and commerce minister, headed that of Laos.
The two sides "discussed in detail the practical items of bilateral cooperation" in those areas and signed a protocol at the end of the session, the report said.
North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song met Kommasith and other Lao officials for talks that the KCNA said were held "in a friendly atmosphere."
Ju Chang-il, a secretary of the Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK), met the delegation of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party led by Anouphab Tounalom, a secretary of the party's central committee.
The Lao delegation visited the Kumsusan Palace of the Sun, where it signed the visitors' book.
In October last year, North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and Lao President Thongloun Sisoulith met during celebrations for the 80th founding anniversary of the North's ruling party and agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation.
The Lao president was one of the few foreign leaders at the event, which included a military parade.
North Korea and Laos have maintained friendly ties since establishing diplomatic relations in 1974.
